projectContext.description: voiceover-matcher-subtitle: AI-powered pipeline for matching voiceover to stock footage

userStories.title: Generate sprint stories for architecture focus area
acceptanceCriteria: Read scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json to understand the 'architecture' focus area
Read scripts/ralph/session/prompt.md for project context and architecture notes
Read scripts/ralph/state/queue.json for interview details (story outline, architecture decisions, key files)
Read CLAUDE.md for project conventions and known issues
Analyze the codebase to find 8-12 specific improvements for 'architecture'
Add stories US-57-002 through US-57-012 to scripts/ralph/state/prd.json (MUST use sprint-prefixed IDs)
Each story MUST have 4-6 testable acceptance criteria
Each story MUST have a 'notes' field with: (1) tier classification, (2) exact source file paths, (3) line number ranges if removing/moving code
IMPORTANT: All generated stories MUST have passes set to false - do NOT run tests or evaluate whether they already pass

Mark this story (US-57-001) as passes: true when done
userStories.notes: Seed story. Generated 11 architecture stories (US-57-002 through US-57-012) based on user interview context (corrupted match data, version check, cookie validation) and codebase exploration of cross-cutting architectural concerns.

userStories.title: Add batch-level diagnostics for corrupted match data during checkpoint restore
acceptanceCriteria: restore_matches_from_dicts() in src/state.py aggregates validation failures and emits a single summary log line: '{n} of {total} match entries have empty source_file (likely all gap matches)' instead of individual ValueError per entry
When >50% of match entries fail validation, log a WARNING with actionable advice: 'Re-run MATCH stage with --match-only'
Validation errors are still collected individually but logged as DEBUG level, not ERROR
Add a test that passes 100 match dicts with 80 having empty source_file and verifies the summary log message appears exactly once
Add a test that passes match dicts with all valid source_file and verifies no summary warning is emitted
userStories.notes: Tier: High priority fix from user interview. Implemented: restore_matches_from_dicts now counts empty_source_count separately, logs individual errors at DEBUG, emits single summary WARNING with counts, and advises --match-only when >50% fail. 4 new tests in TestBatchDiagnostics class. Files modified: src/state.py, tests/test_match_serialization.py.

userStories.title: Centralize checkpoint version constant and fix false-positive version warning
acceptanceCriteria: Define CURRENT_CHECKPOINT_VERSION = '2.0' as a module-level constant in src/checkpoint.py
The checkpoint write path uses CURRENT_CHECKPOINT_VERSION instead of any hardcoded string when setting the version field
The version validation check (around line 528) compares against CURRENT_CHECKPOINT_VERSION instead of hardcoded '1.0'
Add a test that creates a checkpoint with the current version and verifies no version warning is logged during validation
Add a test that creates a checkpoint with version '1.0' and verifies a migration/upgrade notice is logged (not a false alarm)
userStories.notes: Tier: High priority fix from user interview. Source files: src/checkpoint.py (line 528 for version check, and the write path that sets data.version). The current code compares against '1.0' but current checkpoints are written with version '2.0', causing every validation to emit a misleading warning. Single constant eliminates drift between write and validation.

userStories.title: Add startup validation for cookies_from_browser PATH availability
acceptanceCriteria: When download config has cookies_from_browser set, validate at pipeline startup (before any stage runs) that the specified browser executable is findable via shutil.which or platform-appropriate lookup

On validation failure, log a clear WARNING: 'cookies_from_browser is set to "{browser}" but it is not found on PATH. Tier 3 cookie extraction will fail. Set download.cookies_path instead or install {browser}.'
Validation does NOT block pipeline startup — it is a warning, not an error (pipeline can still work without Tier 3)
Add a test that mocks shutil.which to return None for the configured browser and verifies the warning is emitted
Add a test that mocks shutil.which to return a path and verifies no warning is emitted
userStories.notes: Tier: High priority fix from user interview. Source files: src/downloader/core.py (browser detection around lines 185-241), src/pipeline.py (startup validation around lines 136-183). The user had cookies_from_browser: firefox configured but Firefox not on PATH, causing silent Tier 3 failures. Early warning prevents debugging 403 errors that trace back to missing browser.

userStories.title: Extract create_gap_match factory function to eliminate scattered gap match creation
acceptanceCriteria: Create a create_gap_match(vo_segment, reason: str) -> Match function in src/matching/tiered_matcher.py that encapsulates gap match construction with voiceover_segment=vo_segment, video_segment=vo_segment, confidence=0.0
All gap match creation sites in tiered_matcher.py (at least 3 locations around lines 606, 639, 646) use the factory function instead of inline Match() construction
The factory function sets a is_gap_match=True flag or match_type='gap' attribute on the returned Match for downstream identification
Add a test that verifies create_gap_match returns a Match with confidence=0.0 and the gap marker attribute
Add a test that verifies the gap match's video_segment is the same object as voiceover_segment (self-reference pattern)
userStories.notes: Tier: Medium priority refactor. Source files: src/matching/tiered_matcher.py (lines 606-613, 639-646 — three inline gap match constructions). Sprint 45 cleaned up legacy stage references; this continues architectural cleanup in the matching subsystem. Gap matches are a distinct concept that should have a single creation point for consistent behavior.

userStories.title: Extract match serialization logic into shared MatchSerializer utility
acceptanceCriteria: Create a MatchSerializer class or module-level function serialize_match_to_dict(match) in src/matching/ that extracts the common serialization logic from src/stages/match.py lines 171-217
Both MATCH and ITERATIVE_MATCH stage checkpoint serialization paths use the shared serializer instead of duplicated inline logic
The serializer handles both primary_match (MatchResult) and direct video_segment (Match) formats via a single code path
Add a test that serializes a Match with a valid video_segment and verifies source_file, video_start, video_end are present in the output dict
Add a test that serializes a gap match (empty source_file) and verifies the serializer does not raise — returns the dict with empty source_file
userStories.notes: Tier: Medium priority refactor. Source files: src/stages/match.py (lines 171-217, serialize path with duplicate primary_match vs video_segment branches), src/stages/iterative_match.py (similar serialization around lines 419-431). The current duplication means bug fixes to serialization must be applied in two places. Shared serializer enforces consistent checkpoint format.

userStories.title: Split download_segments main loop into focused sub-methods
acceptanceCriteria: The main download loop in src/stages/download_segments.py (lines 540-897) is refactored into sub-methods: _prepare_download_context(), _check_preconditions(), _execute_download(), _handle_result()
Each sub-method is no longer than 80 lines
The main loop body calls the sub-methods sequentially and reads as a high-level narrative of the download process
All existing tests in tests/test_download_segment*.py continue to pass without modification
Add at least one test for _check_preconditions() that verifies circuit breaker open state returns a skip reason
userStories.notes: Tier: Medium priority refactor. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py (lines 540-897, the 357-line download loop). The loop currently mixes candidate filtering, circuit breaker checks, escalation decisions, retry queue management, progress callbacks, and error classification. Extract into sub-methods following single responsibility principle. Do NOT change behavior — pure structural refactor.

userStories.title: Extract error pattern categories in error classification module
acceptanceCriteria: Restructure NETWORK_FAILURE_PATTERNS and similar pattern tuples in src/downloader/error_classification.py (lines 22-40) into a categorized dict: ERROR_PATTERNS = {'dns': [...], 'tcp': [...], 'tls': [...], 'http': [...]}
classify_error_severity() uses the categorized structure and includes the error sub-category in its return value or log output
The flat tuple interface is preserved as a computed property or module-level constant derived from the categorized dict for backward compatibility
Add a test that verifies 'getaddrinfo failed' is classified under the 'dns' sub-category
Add a test that verifies 'HTTP Error 403' is classified under the 'http' sub-category
Add a test that verifies the flattened pattern tuple contains all patterns from all categories
userStories.notes: Tier: Medium priority refactor. Source files: src/downloader/error_classification.py (lines 22-40 for pattern lists, lines 160-192 for classify_error_severity). Currently patterns are flat tuples with no sub-categorization, making error reports less informative. Categorized structure enables better diagnostics (e.g., 'DNS errors: 3, HTTP errors: 12') without changing classification behavior.

userStories.title: Extract circuit breaker pause calculation into composable strategy
acceptanceCriteria: Extract _get_effective_pause_seconds() logic in src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py (lines 160-223) into separate methods: _base_pause(), _escalation_adjusted_pause(), _budget_adjusted_pause()
Extract _cap_pause_duration(pause: float) -> float method used by both _get_effective_pause_seconds and _apply_jitter to eliminate duplicated capping logic (lines 225-270)
The combined pause calculation produces identical results to the current implementation for all code paths
Add a test that verifies pause capping is consistent between the effective pause and jitter paths (same max_pause applied)
Add a test that verifies escalation tier increases the pause duration proportionally
userStories.notes: Tier: Low priority refactor. Source files: src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py (lines 160-270). The current implementation has pause calculation logic interleaved with escalation and budget checks, plus duplicated capping logic between _get_effective_pause_seconds and _apply_jitter. Extracting into composable methods improves testability without changing behavior.

userStories.title: Add STAGE_FIELD_MAP auto-generation from CheckpointData dataclass
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the manually-maintained STAGE_FIELD_MAP dict in src/checkpoint.py (lines 42-50) with an auto-generated mapping derived from CheckpointData dataclass field annotations or a decorator
The auto-generation mechanism maps stage names (e.g., 'ANALYZE') to their corresponding CheckpointData field names (e.g., 'analyze') using a consistent naming convention
Add a validation check at module load time that asserts every entry in STAGE_ORDER has a corresponding field in CheckpointData, raising ImportError if not
Add a test that verifies STAGE_FIELD_MAP contains entries for all stages in STAGE_ORDER
Add a test that verifies adding a stage to STAGE_ORDER without a corresponding CheckpointData field raises an error
userStories.notes: Tier: Low priority improvement. Source files: src/checkpoint.py (lines 42-50 for STAGE_FIELD_MAP, STAGE_ORDER list). Sprint 45 story US-45-007 added sync validation between checkpoint.py and ralph-config.json; this story extends that principle to the internal STAGE_FIELD_MAP -> CheckpointData relationship. Prevents drift when adding new pipeline stages.

userStories.title: Extract magic number constants from state restoration and matching
acceptanceCriteria: Extract DEFAULT_MATCH_DURATION_SECONDS = 10.0 constant from the hardcoded fallback in src/state.py line 146 (video_end = video_start + 10.0)
Extract DEFAULT_GAP_CONFIDENCE = 0.0 constant used in gap match creation in src/matching/tiered_matcher.py
All usage sites reference the named constants instead of inline numeric literals
Add a test that verifies restore_matches_from_dicts uses DEFAULT_MATCH_DURATION_SECONDS when video_end is missing from match data
Each constant has a docstring or inline comment explaining when the fallback triggers
userStories.notes: Tier: Low priority cleanup. Source files: src/state.py (line 146 for 10.0 fallback), src/matching/tiered_matcher.py (lines 606-613 for 0.0 confidence). Magic numbers scattered across restoration and matching logic make it unclear what the defaults represent and where they came from. Named constants document intent and make future changes safer.

userStories.title: Split pipeline config validation into schema validation and runtime environment checks
acceptanceCriteria: Split _validate_config() in src/pipeline.py (lines 136-183) into two methods: _validate_config_schema() (pure config checks, no I/O) and _validate_runtime_environment() (filesystem/PATH checks)
_validate_config_schema() can be called without any filesystem access and validates required fields, type constraints, and value ranges
_validate_runtime_environment() checks cache_dir writability, browser availability, and other I/O-dependent preconditions
Both methods return List[str] of validation errors, and the caller combines them
Add a test that calls _validate_config_schema() with an invalid config and verifies errors are returned without touching the filesystem
userStories.notes: Tier: Low priority refactor. Source files: src/pipeline.py (lines 136-183, _validate_config method). Sprint 45 story US-45-010 moved config validation before checkpoint loading; this story refines the validation itself by separating pure schema checks from I/O-dependent environment checks. Schema validation can run in CI without a real filesystem, enabling faster feedback.
